[Problem]{.card-kicker} **Top K Frequent Elements** [LC 347 · Top K Frequent Elements](https://leetcode.com/problems/top-k-frequent-elements/){difficulty="Medium"}

Sorting values by frequency is $O(n \log n)$. But frequencies are themselves small integers in $[1, n]$, so invert the buckets: index an array *by count* and store the values having that count. Walking the buckets from $n$ down collects the most common values first — stop after $k$. No comparisons; total $O(n)$. This is @sec-lts-p3-a's idea, cut short.

[Solved in full in @sec-lts-p3-b.]{.card-link}
